claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA has a ductile FCC matrix with B2/FCC phase boundaries.
The as-cast state has no significant L12 ordering and has smooth phase boundaries.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 between 550 and 750°C induces L12 ordering and evolution of B2/FCC phase boundaries.
At approximately 600°C, L12 domains in the FCC matrix approach a stoichiometric Ni3Al-like composition and attain a critical degree of order.
Increasing the degree of L12 order toward the proposed 600°C state maximizes the antiphase-boundary energy.
High APBE in the L12 precipitates suppresses dislocation cross-slip.
Jagged or serrated B2/FCC interfaces act as geometric stress concentrators.
The combination of high APBE and jagged B2/FCC interfaces forces dislocations into planar slip bands.
Planar slip produces localized strain and crack initiation at interface serrations, causing intergranular brittleness.
At approximately 750°C, thermal exposure lowers the L12 long-range order parameter and consequently lowers APBE.
Aging at approximately 750°C smooths the B2/FCC interfaces or creates chemically graded ductile transition zones along them.
Reduced ordering and smoother or graded interfaces at 750°C permit cross-slip and restore homogeneous deformation and ductility.
Cross-slip ceases to be completely suppressed when the L12 order parameter falls below approximately 0.6-0.7.
The brittle state requires an L12 order parameter above approximately 0.7 together with a B2/FCC serration amplitude greater than 50 nm.
Tensile elongation has a distinct minimum after aging at approximately 600°C.
The 600°C-aged material will have higher nanoindentation hardness and a lower pop-in load than the 750°C-aged material.
A lower nanoindentation pop-in load is indicative of planar slip in this alloy.
High APBE of L12 ordered precipitates can contribute to strengthening in an FCC-matrix high-entropy alloy.
HEAs can decompose into multiple phases when annealing temperature is changed.

contradictions.description: The boundary field assigns an order-parameter threshold of about 0.7 and a serration threshold greater than 50 nm, while the uncertainty field states that the exact critical order parameter and geometric threshold are not quantified by the available evidence.

The hypothesis describes transition on crossing the order threshold or on a shift in interface-energy anisotropy, whereas the boundary field requires both order above about 0.7 and serration amplitude above 50 nm for brittleness.
